description:
Redwood Inference will implement a prototype mixed-workload scheduling policy for the serving runtime, specifically optimizing the prefill/decode scheduler to handle realistic mixtures of short and long prompts without sacrificing tail latency or throughput. The primary goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency for short prompts while maintaining (or improving) overall tokens/sec and fairness for long prompts, under continuous batching and KV-cache constraints.

Scope includes: (1) defining workload models (prompt-length distributions, arrival processes, concurrency) that represent key customer traffic; (2) implementing one or more scheduling policies (e.g., age-based fairness, quota/virtual-time, or two-queue prefill vs decode prioritization) in the runtime scheduler; (3) adding instrumentation to attribute queuing delay, prefill stalls, decode jitter, and KV-cache pressure; (4) building a benchmark plan and running controlled experiments across at least two GPU SKUs and at least one flagship model family; and (5) preparing a safe rollout plan behind a feature flag with canary metrics and rollback thresholds.

Non-goals: changing model quality, introducing new API surface area, or broad kernel rewrites (kernel changes may occur only if required to support scheduling hooks/metrics). The prototype should integrate with existing observability standards and be compatible with Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Key stakeholders: Runtime Scheduling (Sofia Ivanova, Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Julian Moore), Runtime Kernels (Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato) for any kernel/launch implications, Performance Benchmarks (Rina Kobayashi) for harness and reporting, SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Rafael Mendes) for SLO-aligned metrics and canarying, Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer) for gating/CI reliability, and Product (Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop) for customer-impact framing and acceptable trade-offs.

Proposed timeline (6–8 weeks): Week 1 discovery + requirements and baseline; Weeks 2–4 implementation + instrumentation; Weeks 4–6 benchmarking + tuning; Weeks 6–8 guarded canary in perf-canary and optional limited Hosted rollout. Deliverables include a design doc + ADR(s), benchmark report, implementation PRs, dashboards/alerts updates, and a rollout/playbook.

files.description: Project umbrella: “Mixed-workload prefill/decode scheduler prototype”. Problem statement, success metrics (p95/p99 TTFT, TPOT, throughput), scope/non-goals, and links to design doc, benchmark plan, and tracking sub-issues.
Implement scheduler policy behind feature flag. Acceptance criteria include correctness, no starvation, configurable knobs, and integration with existing continuous batching queue.
Add scheduler instrumentation: queue time breakdown (prefill wait vs decode wait), per-request virtual time/age, and KV-cache pressure signals exported as metrics.
Benchmark suite updates: mixed prompt-length distributions, arrival patterns, and standardized run configs; add reporting for short-vs-long latency tradeoffs.
Canary/rollout plan: enable in perf-canary, define guardrail metrics, rollback thresholds, and SRE signoff checklist.
PM companion ticket: define customer-facing framing and which workload mixes map to Hosted vs Dedicated tiers; confirm acceptable fairness/throughput tradeoffs and release notes expectations.
Primary design doc: background on prefill/decode behavior, proposed policy options, chosen approach, algorithm details (queues, priority function, fairness), configuration knobs, and failure modes.
ADR documenting the selected scheduling policy and why alternatives (pure SRPT, strict priority, naive round-robin) were rejected; includes compatibility and operational considerations.
Benchmark methodology: datasets/prompts, distributions (e.g., bimodal short/long), concurrency levels, hardware matrix, warmup rules, statistical treatment, and how to compare against baseline.
Playbook for debugging regressions: which traces/metrics to inspect, how to reproduce locally, interpreting queue-time histograms, and common pitfalls (KV fragmentation, batch formation pathologies).
Dashboard spec: panels for TTFT/TPOT split by request class, queue delay breakdown, fairness indicators, and feature-flag segmentation; alert recommendations for canary.
SRE guardrails for scheduler experiments: required SLO checks, error budget considerations, and minimum monitoring coverage prior to turning on the flag in production.
Core runtime change: introduce new scheduling policy module and feature flag wiring; includes tests, config docs, and initial reviewers from Runtime Scheduling and SRE.
Instrumentation PR: export scheduler queue-time metrics, per-class latency histograms, and tracing spans around batch formation and decode loops.
Benchmark-lab updates: add mixed-workload scenario generator, standardized configs, and result summarization scripts for short/long split reporting.
perf-canary integration: add canary job that runs baseline vs new scheduler on a fixed matrix and posts regressions; includes threshold logic and Slack notifications.
Observability pack changes: new dashboard JSON / alert rules for scheduler metrics, plus documentation on how to slice by feature flag and request class.
Runtime thread coordinating design choices for short-vs-long prioritization; back-and-forth on starvation risks, knobs, and how to classify requests (prompt length vs predicted decode).
Thread with Applied ML / evals asking whether scheduler changes could alter output timing/streaming behavior; confirms no quality impact but calls out streaming jitter metrics to watch.
SRE review thread: canary plan, required dashboards, and rollback criteria; includes links to perf-canary PR and guardrail doc.
Architecture thread: discussion on whether the new policy should become a general “policy framework” vs a single implementation; agrees on minimal abstraction for prototype.
Engineer working doc: scratch notes on experimental runs, parameter sweeps, unexpected pathologies, and links to raw benchmark outputs.
Results write-up: charts/tables comparing baseline vs new scheduler across workload mixes and GPUs; includes interpretation, caveats, and recommended default knobs.
Email requesting cross-team review (SRE, Product, Release Eng) of the design doc and canary plan; includes timeline and specific review questions.
Email thread confirming SRE approval to run perf-canary and limited production canary under defined thresholds; includes who is on point and rollback authority.
